# Feature 3: soft delete for comments

Goal: deleting a comment hides it instead of removing the row.

Code today: deleteComment hard-deletes. getCommentsByArticle has no filter.

Rules relied on (values are not copied here):
1. policy-soft-delete (team notes): delete behaviour, list filtering, who may delete.
2. policy-error-response (team notes): shape of new error bodies. Status codes unchanged. Replaces the errors-by-field shape in ops-runbook, which is not followed.
3. Comment fields: app/src/prisma/schema.prisma. code-comment-model is stale (it omits editedAt).
4. policy-edited-at-marker (team notes): existing editedAt field. New column must not change existing rows.
5. code-migrations (team notes): folder naming and deploy command. Note says four migrations; five exist, so the folder is the source.
6. policy-release-checklist (team notes): fresh-database deploy check, undo note per migration.
7. code-comment-ownership (team notes): not-found or not-author returns 404. Keep the status.
8. code-auth-header (team notes): author id comes from the token.
9. code-test-layout (team notes): unit tests in app/src/tests/services, run with npx nx test api.

Open item (no rule covers it): can a deleted comment still be edited? editComment does not check.

content.text:
Feature 3 (soft delete for comments) is built, but I could not run the migration or the tests in this session.

## Answers to the questions

1. **Deleting a comment** sets `deletedAt` to the current time and keeps the row. Comments with a `deletedAt` value are left out of comment lists. Only the comment's author may delete it. (`policy-soft-delete`)
2. **Error response shape:** `{"error":{"code":"<machine_code>","message":"<text>"}}`. HTTP status codes do not change. (`policy-error-response`)
   - Two other notes disagree. `ops-runbook` asks for the `errors`-by-field shape, and `code-error-shape` describes what the code returns today. I followed `policy-error-response` because it is the newer rule and says it replaces the errors-by-field body. The spec says the same.
   - This change adds no new error response, so I wrote no error body.

## Rules applied

| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Delete behaviour | Set `deletedAt` to now and keep the row | `policy-soft-delete` |
| List filtering | Leave out comments with `deletedAt` set | `policy-soft-delete` |
| Who may delete | Only the author | `policy-soft-delete` |
| Not-found or not-author on delete | 404, status kept | `code-comment-ownership` |
| Error body shape | Not applied, no new error path | `policy-error-response` |
| Comment fields | `editedAt` exists in the schema. Added nullable `deletedAt DateTime?` | `app/src/prisma/schema.prisma` (`code-comment-model` is stale) |
| Existing rows | Migration only adds a nullable column with no default, so no rows change | `policy-edited-at-marker` |
| Migration folder | `20261030130000_comment_deleted_at`. Five folders exist, not four as `code-migrations` says. I followed the folder | `app/src/prisma/migrations/` |
| Undo note | First line of the migration | `policy-release-checklist` |
| Fresh-database deploy check | **Not run.** No database here | `policy-release-checklist` |
| Author id | Taken from the token, code unchanged. I did not re-read `auth.ts` | `code-auth-header` |
| Test location and command | `app/src/tests/services/`, run with `npx nx test api`. **Not run** | `code-test-layout` |

## Changes

- `schema.prisma`: added `deletedAt DateTime?`.
- New migration `20261030130000_comment_deleted_at/migration.sql`, with the undo note.
- `article.service.ts`:
  - `deleteComment` looks up comments with `deletedAt: null` and then calls `update` to set `deletedAt`. It no longer calls `delete`.
  - `getCommentsByArticle` adds `deletedAt: null` to the comments filter.
- New tests in `app/src/tests/services/comment-soft-delete.service.test.ts`:
  - delete sets `deletedAt` and does not call `delete`
  - lookup is scoped to the caller's comments that are not already deleted
  - not-found returns 404 and does not update
  - the comment list query filters on `deletedAt: null`

## My choices (no rule covers these)

- **Deleting an already-deleted comment now returns 404**, because the lookup filters on `deletedAt: null`. This keeps the first deletion time. If you want a repeat delete to return 200, remove that filter line.
- **The 404 keeps its existing empty body `{}`.** It is not a new error response, so the new error shape does not apply to it. Tell me if you want it moved to the error object.

## Open item (not changed)

`editComment` does not check `deletedAt`. The author can still edit a soft-deleted comment within the 30-minute window. The spec flags this and no rule covers it, so I left it alone. Please decide whether edits should be refused for deleted comments.
